title: High-Alert Meds: Blood Thinners, Insulin, Opioids

questions.stem: A client receives too much heparin. Which antidote should the nurse expect?
questions.explanation: C is correct: protamine sulfate reverses heparin. A, vitamin K, reverses warfarin. B, naloxone, reverses opioids. D is not a heparin antidote.

questions.stem: Which lab does the nurse monitor for a client on a heparin infusion?
questions.explanation: B is correct: heparin goes with the partial thromboplastin time. A goes with warfarin. C and D aren't the heparin lab taught.

questions.stem: A client on warfarin has a high international normalized ratio. Which antidote may be ordered?
questions.explanation: B is correct: vitamin K reverses warfarin. A reverses heparin. C reverses opioids. D is not a warfarin antidote.

questions.stem: A client on warfarin for most conditions asks about the lab goal. Which international normalized ratio is often the goal?
questions.explanation: C is correct: the international normalized ratio goal is often 2 to 3. A and B are too low for treatment. D is too high and raises bleeding risk.

questions.stem: Which teaching is correct for a client on a blood thinner? Select all that apply.

options.text: Stop eating all leafy greens on warfarin

questions.explanation: A, B, C, and D are correct: soft toothbrush, electric razor, and watching for bleeding like bruising, nosebleeds, and black stools. E is wrong: on warfarin, keep vitamin K foods steady; don't stop them or suddenly eat much more.

questions.stem: Which insulin is the only one given into a vein?
questions.explanation: B is correct: regular insulin is the only one given into a vein. A and C are not. D is wrong for the same reason.

questions.stem: A client receives rapid-acting insulin. When should the client eat?
questions.explanation: A is correct: rapid-acting insulin starts in about 15 minutes, so the client should eat within 15 minutes. B, C, and D risk low blood sugar.

questions.stem: Which statement about insulin pens is correct?

options.text: Pens can be shared if the needle is changed
Pens can be shared within a family
Pens can be shared in the hospital only

questions.explanation: B is correct: never share pens. A, C, and D all allow sharing.

questions.stem: A client on an opioid has a breathing rate of 8 and is very sleepy. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Stop the opioid, try to wake the client, support breathing, and give naloxone as ordered
Give the next opioid dose early

questions.explanation: B is correct: a breathing rate below about 12 with heavy sleepiness means stop the opioid, try to wake them, support breathing, and give naloxone, as ordered. A delays care. C and D give more opioid.

questions.stem: Which side effect of opioids should the nurse teach about in addition to slowed breathing?
questions.explanation: B is correct: the nurse also teaches about constipation. A, C, and D are not the side effect taught.
